prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an L-shaped checkout counter extending from the immediate foreground (0.3–0.6 m, brightest white) to about 1.2–1.5 m on the left, with a standing person across the counter at roughly 0.8–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer and a pastry display case at 1.5–2.2 m on the right. On the counter within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the other person are a register keypad at the bottom-left (0.4–0.6 m), a red plastic shopping basket at the bottom-right in frames 1–3 (0.4–0.7 m) that is moved onto the left counter wing (1.0–1.2 m) in front of a upright brown paper bag (1.1–1.4 m) by frame 5, and counter jars on the far left (0.5–0.8 m). Across the 5 frames, the person faces the counter and camera wearer while leaning forward in frame 1 so their right arm reaches 0.5 m at the keypad, stepping slightly back to ~1.0–1.2 m in frames 2–3 while reaching their left hand to the basket at the right edge, turning slightly left toward the bag in frame 4 (~0.9 m), and standing upright at ~0.9–1.1 m facing forward and slightly left in frame 5 with their lower body occluded by the counter Throughout. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the continuous distance gradient along the L-shaped counter surfaces, the recessed gap behind the counter where the person stands, and the step in depth between the red basket and the paper bag behind it in frame 5. However, the map is unreliable around the open lattice holes of the red basket in frame 2 (which bleed background depth), softens the keypad and jar contours into indistinct blobs, and clips the background hallway and doorway beyond 2.5 m to uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the standing person in front of the counter (roughly 0.8–1.2 m from the camera wearer) as a pink mask across all 5 frames, while labeling the register keypad at the bottom-left (0.4–0.6 m, within arm's reach) as 'laptop' in frame 1 and 'keyboard' in frame 3, and the elevated glass display case on the right (1.5–2.2 m, ~1.0 m to the person's left) as 'tv' in frames 2 and 4. Across the sequence, the person's mask shifts from leaning left with an extended right arm overlapping the top edge of the register mask in frame 1, to standing centrally with the head cropped by the top frame boundary in frames 2–4 and the left arm extending to the right frame edge in frame 3, to occupying the right side of the frame in frame 5 as they turn slightly toward the left counter. The masks capture how the counter edge occludes the person's lower torso and legs from below in every frame, while the top image border cuts off the person's head in frames 1–4 before their head and glasses re-enter the frame in frame 5 looking downward toward the counter rather than directly at the camera wearer. Compared to motion-blurred RGB frames (especially frame 1), segmentation provides sharp outer boundaries for the person's torso and reaching arm relative to the register surface. However, it is highly unreliable for scene completeness and classification: it completely misses the L-shaped counter, the red basket, and the brown paper bag, drops the register in frames 2, 4, and 5 and the display case in frames 1, 3, and 5, misclassifies the register and display case as 'laptop'/'keyboard' and 'tv', and leaves hollow black holes inside the person's jacket and white shirt in frames 2 and 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, capturing only a magenta right hand at the bottom-left in frame 1 (~0.5 m from the camera wearer) and near the center-left counter in frame 3 (~0.8 m), alongside yellow upper-body skeletons for the person in frames 2 and 5 (~0.9–1.2 m away) and a mislocalized yellow cluster on the right in frame 4. In frames 2 and 5, the shoulder, hip, and facial keypoints show the person standing behind the counter facing generally toward the camera wearer and angled slightly to the left, with their head tilted downward toward the counter surface rather than looking into the lens, and their lower body below the hips occluded by the counter. In frame 1, the magenta finger keypoints explicitly trace the person's right hand flat against the register keypad within arm's reach of both people, while in frame 2 the yellow arm segments show the right arm hanging down near the counter gap and the left arm bent near the red basket, and in frame 3 the magenta hand keypoints mark the right fist resting on the counter surface. Even when the person's dark jacket sleeves blend into the dark background or suffer motion blur in RGB, the pose map pinpoints exact joint articulations, finger orientations on the keypad, and head/eye landmarks in frames 2 and 5. However, the pose map is spatially unreliable across much of the strip: it misses the entire body skeleton in frames 1 and 3, fails to detect the person's left arm reaching for the basket in frame 3, misses the hands in frames 2, 4, and 5, and hallucinates a sideways yellow body skeleton on the glass pastry case (~1.8 m away on the right) in frame 4 while missing the actual person standing at the center-left.
